title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps

epigraph.quote: A great insurer earns a premium book multiple only when normalized combined ratios and float returns clear the cost of equity with ample margin of safety.
epigraph.author: Insurance Valuation Desk Maxim

web_blocks.title: 7.1 Deconstructing $231.39: Peak Trailing ROE vs. Normalizing Forward Earnings

web_blocks.html: At the November 20, 2026 close of $231.39, Progressive carries a $133.67 billion market capitalization on 577.7 million shares outstanding [25, 28]. Shares trade at 11.65x trailing earnings ($19.85 TTM EPS), 14.44x forward earnings, 8.78x free cash flow, and 3.89x Q3 book value ($3.74x October 31 book value of $61.90 per share) [25, 28]. At first glance, 11.65x trailing earnings and 8.78x free cash flow look inexpensive against the S&P 500. Yet Wall Street's consensus target sits at just $236.95, offering only +2.40% implied upside [25].

That narrow +2.40% consensus spread explains the valuation paradox. Forward P/E rises from 11.65x trailing to 14.44x forward because consensus models a -12.82% drop in next-year EPS (roughly $16.02 per share) and -4.17% five-year EPS growth [25]. Why? Through October 2026, Progressive delivered a peak 87.9% YTD combined ratio and 34.4% TTM ROE [28]. Yet the November 18, 2026 Form 8-K revealed October companywide CR jumping to 91.2% and Direct Auto CR hitting 96.1%, breaching management's 96.0% ceiling [28]. Meanwhile, Q3 advertising surged 18% YoY to $1.6 billion while personal auto Policy Life Expectancy fell 9% YoY and Direct Auto PIF stalled at 16,846 thousand [28, 29, 30].

Pass 1 forensics also uncovered a critical structural cap. Progressive's $1.2 billion Florida policyholder credit in FY2025 was not voluntary goodwill; Florida's statutory three-accident-year excess-profit limit forced the refund [32]. With Texas (12.4%) and Florida (12.3%) representing 24.7% of FY2025 net premiums written, statutory rules cap supernormal underwriting windfalls while rising PIP severity (+16% YoY), tariffs, and zero auto catastrophe reinsurance keep downside tail risk open [29, 31, 32].

web_blocks.title: 7.2 Excess-Return Model & Normalized 91.8% Combined Ratio Fair Value

web_blocks.html: We value Progressive using a two-stage Excess-Return model on October 31, 2026 common equity ($35,757 million, or $61.90 per share across 577.7 million shares) [28]. Standard EV/EBITDA fails because insurance float is an operating liability, while total debt rose to $8,389 million (19.0% debt-to-capital) after March 2026's $1.5 billion Senior Notes issuance [28, 29]. Investors at $231.39 pay $97.91 billion above book value for future returns above a 9.5% cost of equity.

Rather than anchoring to FY2025's peak 87.4% combined ratio, we calibrate normalized economics to Pass 1's 2026 trajectory. Written and earned premium growth slowed to +4% and +5% YoY in Q3 2026, while Direct Auto PIF stalled sequentially in October at a 96.1% combined ratio [4, 28, 30]. Modeling a 5.0% 10-year NPE CAGR (FY2027–FY2036) and a normalized **91.8% combined ratio** (8.2% underwriting margin) alongside a 4.2% investment yield on $100B+ float yields ~$9.02 billion in FY2027E net income ($15.75 per share post-buybacks). Over the decade, average ROE settles near **23.5%** (versus 34.4% TTM peak) [28].

Discounting those excess returns at a 9.5% cost of equity (4.25% risk-free rate plus 5.25% equity risk premium) with 4.5% terminal growth yields a Base fair value of **$242.00 per share** (3.91x October book value, 15.1x NTM EPS). From $231.39 CMP, $242.00 implies just +4.59% upside—only **0.54:1 reward-to-risk** against the $211.78 snapshot stop ($19.61 risk). Even on a pullback to the 10-week EMA ($225.19), reward-to-risk reaches only **1.25:1**, still below our 1.50:1 hurdle.

web_blocks.the_number: $242.00 per share Base intrinsic value (+4.59% vs. $231.39 CMP; 3.91x Oct 31 BVPS of $61.90; 15.1x NTM $16.02 EPS).
web_blocks.how_calculated: Two-stage Excess-Return (Residual Income) model discounting 10-year projected ROE minus 9.5% cost of equity plus a 4.5% terminal-growth Gordon value on $35,757M starting equity.
web_blocks.the_inputs: 5.0% NPE CAGR (FY2027–FY2036), 91.8% normalized combined ratio (8.2% UW margin), 4.2% pretax float yield, $375M annual interest on $8,389M debt, 20.5% tax rate, 9.5% Ke, 4.5% terminal g.
web_blocks.the_range: Bear $188.00 (25% prob; 94.5% CR, 3.0% NPE CAGR) | Base $242.00 (55% prob; 91.8% CR, 5.0% NPE CAGR) | Bull $285.00 (20% prob; 89.5% CR, 6.5% NPE CAGR). Probability-weighted EV: $237.10 (+2.47%).
web_blocks.if_off: If Direct Auto's 96.1% October CR spreads into FY2027 or personal auto price competition forces a 94%+ CR, fair value compresses toward $188.00–$215.00. Conversely, sustaining <89.5% CR without Florida excess-profit refunds lifts fair value toward $285.00.

web_blocks.caption: Excess-Return Sensitivity Matrix: Normalized Combined Ratio vs. NPE Growth (USD/sh)
web_blocks.takeaway: Only an 89.5% combined ratio—170 bps better than October's 91.2% overall and 660 bps better than Direct Auto's 96.1%—justifies $271–$285. At a realistic 91.8% CR, fair value is $242.00.

web_blocks.html: Two Red Team stress adjustments sharpen that valuation discipline [28]. First, YTD October 2026's headline 87.9% combined ratio benefits from $1,674 million of favorable prior-year reserve development—equal to **2.34% of YTD NPE ($71,576M)** and **17.6% of YTD net income ($9,499M)** [28]. Stripping out those reserve releases places Progressive's underlying YTD accident-year combined ratio near **90.2%**, only 160 bps below our 91.8% Base assumption [28]. Second, our Base $242.00 fair value is highly sensitive to terminal growth and float yield: cutting terminal `g` from 4.5% to **3.5%** drops Base fair value to **$206.33/sh (-10.8% vs. $231.39 CMP)**, while cutting pretax float yield 50 bps from 4.2% to **3.7%** trims **-$10.34/sh**—pulling Base to $231.66 and dragging the 94.5% CR Bear Case down to **$177.66/sh (-23.2% vs. CMP)**.

web_blocks.caption: Red Team Excess-Return Sensitivity & Reserve-Release Stress Test (CMP: $231.39)
web_blocks.takeaway: Red Team sensitivity proves $231.39 leaves zero safety margin: at 3.5% terminal growth fair value falls to $206.33 (-10.8%), a 50 bps float-yield drop cuts -$10.34/sh (to $177.66 combined Bear), and ex-PYD underlying CR already sits near 90.2%.

web_blocks.title: 7.3 Peer Benchmarking Across Live November 20, 2026 P&C Snapshots

web_blocks.html: Live TradingView peer data as of November 20, 2026 confirm Progressive's operating quality alongside its rich book multiple [21, 22, 23, 25, 34]. Progressive leads peers on growth (+7.65% TTM revenue) and sits near the top on ROE (33.24%), second only to Allstate's post-recovery 38.92% ROE [23, 25]. Yet Progressive trades at 3.89x book value—double Chubb's 1.94x, 78% above Allstate's 2.19x, and nearly triple RenaissanceRe's 1.32x [21, 23, 25, 34]. On trailing P/E, Progressive (11.65x) is only slightly below Chubb (13.01x) and sits above Travelers (10.31x), RenaissanceRe (9.89x), and Allstate (6.05x) [21, 22, 23, 25, 34].

web_blocks.caption: U.S. P&C Insurance Peer Valuation, Profitability & Stage 2 Matrix (as of Nov 20, 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: Every P&C peer above sits in STAGE_2, yet Progressive's 3.89x book multiple prices in durable >23% ROE at a time when Oct Direct Auto hit a 96.1% combined ratio and Street consensus sees +2.4% upside.

web_blocks.title: Why We Do Not Stretch Normalized Assumptions to Force a Higher Target
paragraphs: To clear 1.50:1 reward-to-risk from the upper snapshot band ($233.59 vs. $211.78 stop), Progressive would need a $266.31 Base target (+12.4% above Wall Street's $236.95 consensus) [25]. Achieving $266+ requires sustaining sub-90% combined ratios despite October Direct Auto hitting 96.1%, PLE dropping 9% YoY, Q3 ad spend jumping 18% YoY, and Florida's statutory excess-profit limit capping windfalls [28, 29, 32]. Unbiased underwriting rejects stretched assumptions.

web_blocks.html: Valuation Upgrade Trigger: Re-underwrite PGR above TIER_0 only if shares pull back to $205.00–$215.00 AND monthly Form 8-K Direct Auto CR stabilizes below 92.0% with intact 40M+ PIF—or at a deeper discount below $190.00–$195.00 if Direct Auto CR remains at or above 92.0% [28].

book_subsections.title: 7.1 Solving the Valuation Puzzle at $231.39
paragraphs: On November 20, 2026, Progressive closed at $231.39, giving the insurer a $133.67 billion market value across 577.7 million shares. At first glance, the stock looks inexpensive at 11.65 times trailing earnings and 8.78 times free cash flow. Yet forward earnings jump to 14.44 times, book value sits at 3.89 times third-quarter equity (3.74 times October 31 book value of $61.90), and Wall Street's consensus price target is only $236.95—just 2.4% above the market price.

Unpack the underwriting cycle and those numbers make complete sense. Trailing earnings of $19.85 per share capture an unusually profitable peak, highlighted by an 87.4% combined ratio in 2025 and 87.9% through October 2026. Analysts expect forward earnings per share to fall roughly 12.8% as auto margins normalize. The November 18 monthly filing underscored that shift: October's companywide combined ratio rose to 91.2%, while Direct Auto surged to 96.1%, briefly breaching management's 96% ceiling. Meanwhile, third-quarter ad spending jumped 18% year over year to $1.6 billion even as personal auto Policy Life Expectancy declined 9%.

Our Pass 1 forensic review also uncovered an underappreciated ceiling on upside surprises. Progressive's $1.2 billion Florida policyholder credit in 2025 was mandated by Florida's statutory three-accident-year excess-profit law, not voluntary generosity. With Texas and Florida generating 24.7% of total net premiums written, statutory limits cap supernormal profits in Florida while tariffs, 16% PIP claim inflation, and un-reinsured auto storm losses preserve downside exposure.

book_subsections.title: 7.2 Normalized Excess-Return Model and Sensitivity Reality
paragraphs: Because insurance float is an operating liability rather than industrial debt, we value Progressive with a two-stage Excess-Return model anchored on October 31 equity of $35.757 billion ($61.90 per share). At $231.39, buyers pay nearly $98 billion above book value for future returns exceeding a 9.5% cost of equity. Note also that debt rose to $8.389 billion after March 2026's $1.5 billion note issuance, while the bond portfolio shifted 47.2% into corporate and structured credit carrying $2.432 billion of net unrealized losses.

Calibrating to Q3 and October 2026 trends, we model a 5.0% annual earned-premium growth rate over ten years—reflecting Q3's slowdown to 4% written and 5% earned growth—paired with a normalized 91.8% combined ratio and a 4.2% investment yield. That yields roughly $9.02 billion in FY2027 net income, or $15.75 per share after buybacks, and a long-run average ROE near 23.5%. Discounting those excess returns at 9.5% with 4.5% terminal growth produces a Base fair value of $242.00 per share, just 4.6% above today's price.

In our scenario tree, a 20%-weighted Bull Case reaches $285.00 if the combined ratio holds 89.5% and premium growth re-accelerates to 6.5%. Our 55%-weighted Base Case sits at $242.00 on a 91.8% combined ratio and 5.0% growth. Our 25%-weighted Bear Case drops to $188.00 if soft-market pricing and claims inflation push the combined ratio to 94.5%. Probability-weighting all three yields $237.10—virtually identical to Wall Street's $236.95 target. At $231.39, you are paying nearly full fair value before accounting for market-regime risk.

Think about why a 4.4-point shift in normalized combined ratio matters so much to per-share value. On roughly $90 billion of earned premiums in 2027, each one-point move in the combined ratio adds or subtracts about $900 million of pre-tax underwriting profit. After taxes, that equals roughly $1.25 per share of annual earnings power. Moving from FY2025's 87.4% trough to a realistic 91.8% cycle average trims nearly $5.50 per share from peak underwriting earnings, which is exactly why forward earnings sit 12.8% below trailing earnings.

Now look at the bond portfolio side of the ledger. Progressive holds $100.166 billion in total investments earning a 4.4% pretax book yield in October 2026, with a conservative 3.6-year duration and AA- average credit quality. Yet in 2026, management rotated out of U.S. Treasuries—cutting government holdings from 54.3% to 41.9%—and raised corporate bonds, asset-backed securities, and mortgage-backed securities to 47.2% of the book. With $2.432 billion of net unrealized fixed-maturity losses already sitting on the balance sheet at October 31, credit spreads add one more reason not to stretch for a rich book multiple.

A Red Team stress check reinforces why $231.39 offers no margin of safety. First, YTD October 2026's headline 87.9% combined ratio includes $1,674 million of favorable prior-year reserve releases—equal to 2.34% of earned premiums and 17.6% of YTD net income—meaning Progressive's underlying accident-year combined ratio already runs near 90.2%. Second, lowering terminal growth from 4.5% to 3.5% drops Base fair value to $206.33 per share (-10.8% below market). Third, a 50-basis-point decline in pretax float yield from 4.2% to 3.7% trims $10.34 per share, pulling Base value down to $231.66 and dropping the 94.5% combined-ratio Bear Case from $188.00 to $177.66 per share (-23.2%).

book_subsections.title: 7.3 Peer Multiples Confirm Quality Without Margin of Safety
paragraphs: Comparing Progressive to Chubb, Travelers, Allstate, and RenaissanceRe as of November 20, 2026 highlights both Progressive's strengths and its thin margin of safety. Progressive grows revenue faster at +7.65% and delivers a 33.24% trailing ROE, trailing only Allstate's 38.92% rebound ROE. All four peers sit alongside Progressive in Stage 2 uptrends.

However, Progressive trades at 3.89 times book value versus 1.94 times at Chubb, 2.78 times at Travelers, 2.19 times at Allstate, and 1.32 times at RenaissanceRe. On trailing earnings, Progressive at 11.65 times actually trades slightly richer than Travelers at 10.31 times and Allstate at 6.05 times, while forward earnings sit at 14.44 times. Paying nearly four times book value for a carrier whose Direct Auto combined ratio just touched 96.1% and whose consensus target sits just 2.4% higher leaves zero room for error.
